newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Blast wounds at least 20 at Albanian cafe.
newsitem.headline: Blast wounds at least 20 at Albanian cafe.

text.p: At least 20 people were injured on Monday when a bomb heavily damaged a cafe on the main square of the Albanian capital Tirana, witnesses said.

The cafe on Skanderberg Square was a known rendezvous point for Socialists, the main opposition to President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party in June 29 elections, called to end turbulence in the impoverished Balkan country.
Witnesses said they saw two young men entering the cafe with a parcel. One of them went to the toilet and a minute later the blast occurred, causing the balcony of the second storey to collapse.
The Cafe Freskia, owned by the Socialist Party leader and state secretary for the Interior Ministry Lush Perpali, was known to be frequented by Socialist supporters.
A story printed in the pro-Berisha newspaper Albania on Sunday carried the headline "Lush Perpali's restaurant will be blown up".
Police immediately sealed off the area surrounding the cafe which adjoins the ministries of defence and mineral resources and opens onto the back court of the Socialist Party headquarters.
A police officer said at least six people had been seriously injured, and that a waiter had apparently suffered the most serious injuries.
An injured customer called Agron said there were some 30 to 50 clients in the cafe at the time of the blast, shortly after midday, and about 20 of them had been injured.
"This is Berisha's typical fundamentalist action because it is well known this cafe is frequented by Socialist supporters," Agron said. "This is a terrorist act."

Agron Shahu, an officer at Tirana's military hospital, said three of the injured had been treated there and released. A nurse at Tirana's Emergency Hospital said 17 victims had been released after treatment while one, Arjan Shameti, who rented the cafe, was being treated for serious injuries.

It was not immediately known what kind of explosive device had been used. Albania has been awash with weapons and all sorts of military ordnance since armouries were looted in March during riots that swept much of the country.
The riots were sparked by thousands of people losing their life savings in the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes.

People blamed Berisha and his Democratic Party-led government for the collapse, forcing Berisha to agree to the formation of a multi-party government of national reconciliation and to hold early elections set for June 29.
